svg.title: We describe the geometry and algebra of that finite matching construction more precisely. Make one copy of the input list in every cell of a fixed coarse tiling, with the prescribed reflection and translation of that cell. Write Fv,i for these copied insertions and qv = Q i Fv,i. The anchor copy is unchanged. At level m + 1 all members of the original list have parent zero, so the parents of the copied list are exactly the tiling centers. At every finer level the copied position has the same coarser parent as its center and lies within half the intervening block length of the embedded parent. Two distinct centers are separated at the parent level by at least B2 m+1+1. If the intervening enlargement factor is L, their embedded separation is at least L(B2 m+1 + 1); the two deviations cost strictly less than L. The propagated budget satisfies B2 i ≤LB2 m+1. The triangle inequality therefore gives the required cross-copy separation at every intermediate level. Within a copy the given finest-level spacing supplies the remaining separation condition.
